thread:
Anya: Heads up — onboarding Thalassa11b (13B) int4 is showing a pretty consistent summarization quality drop vs fp16 on our eval set. Rouge-L down from ~36.2 -> ~31.0. Looks like something around rotary scaling or tokenizer BOS handling.
Mira: Ugh. Any repro artifacts or single-batch logs?
Anya: Pushed a quick smoke to the eval harness, link: https://ci.internal/runs/thalassa-int4-smoke (infra-bot posted job). Metrics + sample diffs in the run. Short summary: int4-nf4 profile vs fp16 baseline. Same prompt seeds.
Sam: Is the tokenizer mapping identical? Last time we had a drift when BOS/CLS was remapped during conversion.
Anya: Tokenizer mapping is *mostly* identical, but Thalassa has a custom BOS at id 1 (not 50256). Conversion script maps it but I noticed some merged tokens with leading U+0120 marker getting different IDs compared to our canonical vocab.
Jesse: Could be merge table ordering. Even a tiny remap changes kv-cache alignment for longprefix. Was this evaluated with prefix caching enabled?
Anya: Yes — prefix caching enabled. I ran a control with caching disabled and Rouge-L improved by ~1.2 points, so cache alignment is suspect.
Mira: That suggests token id offseting: if tokenizer returns new ids, rotor/rotary position encoding may be applied to wrong positions during cache reuse.
Sam: Share the minimal repro code you ran.
Anya: Paste of the harness call:
```bash
# run on a single A100 reserved node
python -m eval.run --model thalassa-13b-int4 --tokenizer thalassa-vocab.json --batch 8 --prefix-cache true --rotary-phase-scale 1.0 --quant-profile nf4
```
Anya: And a small snippet from the model init log that looks suspicious:
```
[init] tokenizer.vocab_size=50288 (converted from hf)
[init] rotary_phase_scale=1.0000
[warn] kv_cache_offset_mismatch: observed_cache_len=512 expected=511
[quant] loaded int4 profile: per-channel scales present=true fallback=false
```
Mira: That kv_cache_offset_mismatch is a red flag. Which conversion path produced the checkpoint? hf->redwood converter?
Anya: Yes: `hf->redwood convert` using converter v0.9.1. I did notice the rotary params serialized as `rotary_scale` in the checkpoint but our runtime expects `rotary_phase_scale` — converter set both but `rotary_phase_scale` got default 1.0 override during loading.
Jesse: That would silently change attention phase amplitude for int4 path if kernel uses that value to select optimized kernels. Int4 kernels sometimes implement a slightly different rotary rescaling for numeric stability.
Sam: Quick hypothesis: converter left a hidden tiny offset in token ids (merge ordering) AND rotary_phase_scale got forced to 1.0 for int4, together producing phase mismatch in cached KV leading to degeneration.
Mira: Plan: 1) re-run with explicit `--rotary-phase-scale` set to the fp16 value (from fp16 checkpoint header) 2) run with `--prefix-cache false` 3) run with a tokenizer sanity check that compares token ids for a fixed set of doc prompts between fp16 and int4.
Anya: I already did (2) and (3) quick checks: with explicit rotary-phase taken from fp16 (1.0234) Rouge-L jumps back +2.8 points (but not fully recovered). With prefix-cache disabled + explicit rotary-phase it's within 0.6 points of baseline.
Sam: Good. So two orthogonal issues: tokenizer id ordering and rotary scalar. Next step: bisect which of those is larger effect.
Mira: For tokenizer ordering, run `python tools/tokenmap_diff.py fp16_vocab.json int4_vocab.json --samples 1000` and produce a histogram of first-differing-index. If differences clustered around small indices -> merge table ordering; if random -> conversion bug.
Anya: Ran tokenmap_diff, attached small excerpt in the run. Most diffs are concentrated at boundary 0-256 and at some Unicode combining char mappings. I suspect our `lexnorm` step during conversion used a different NFKC normalization than the original tokenization.
Jesse: If lexnorm differs, that will change token boundaries and impact cache reuse massively. Could also explain dropout in long-context metrics.
Sam: For immediate mitigation, we can (A) force full-tokenization and compare model outputs without cache to ensure model behavior still matches; (B) add a conversion flag `--preserve-nfkc` to the converter to keep original unicode normalization.
Anya: Created an issue on converter repo: https://git.internal/converter/issue/489 — flagged `preserve-nfkc` and rotary key name mismatch.
Mira: Also add a unit test to runtime loader that asserts `checkpoint.rotary_phase_scale == model.config['rotary_phase_scale']` and fails loudly. Silent defaulting is lethal.
Anya: Agreed. I started a hotfix branch that reads both `rotary_phase_scale` and `rotary_scale` keys and logs a warning if they differ.
infra-bot: Job queued: thalassa-int4-rotary-bisect (id: job-5842). Logs: https://ci.internal/jobs/job-5842/logs
Sam: For the bisect job, include two eval modes: (1) force fp16 rotary_phase into int4 runtime; (2) force int4 tokenizer to use fp16 tokenmap via `--use-tokenmap fp16.map`.
Anya: Doing that now. Also adding a small eval of hallucination rate — earlier I saw some summary hallucinations increase in int4 run.
Mira: Great. Can we prioritize getting a minimal repro sample that shows exact token id sequence, key/value cache snapshots (first 4 steps) and attention weight deltas between fp16 and int4? That will help confirm phase vs id issues.
Jesse: I'll add a short hook into the runtime to dump per-layer rotary phase matrices for first two layers on a single prompt. Keep it small, only for debug builds.
Anya: Thanks. I'll collect outputs and post here once job-5842 completes. Expected ~20m.
Sam: Follow-ups: - converter: add `preserve-nfkc` flag + make rotary key consistent - runtime: fail on missing rotary metadata - eval: run bisect and post top 20 tokens where outputs diverge - devex: patch onboarding checklist to include `tokenmap_diff` step
Anya: Assigning owners: Mira -> runtime warning/test; Jesse -> runtime rotary dump hook; Sam -> converter PR; Anya -> eval bisect and patch onboarding checklist.
Mira: I'll open a runtime PR in the next few hours.
Anya: Thanks all :thumbsup: I'll update when job-5842 finishes with diffs and the exact Rouge deltas per condition.
Sam: If we need a quick rollback path for customers using Dedicated/Private, we can gate the int4 profile behind a feature flag until conversion fixes land.
Anya: Good call. Will prepare a mitigation note for support.
Jesse: job-5842 finished: small parity recovered when forcing fp16 rotary_phase; still investigating remaining ~0.6 R-L gap. Dump artifacts here: https://ci.internal/artifacts/job-5842/dumps.tar.gz
Anya: Got the dumps, starting analysis now.
